Spain were the stronger team in the final and Argentina were damned by their lack of ambition even before they had Enzo Fernández sent off towards the end of the regulation time. — Photograph: Brian Snyder/Reuters

item.description:
London, England — Britain’s Josh Kerr competes in the men’s one-mile event during the IAAF Diamond League athletics at the London stadium. Kerr shattered the one-mile world record in London and became the seventh British man to hold the record, following such greats as Roger Bannister, Lord Coe and Steve Ovett. ‘Absolutely incredible,’ was the verdict of Coe, the World Athletics president. ‘Foot perfect. To go into there with that kind of mental resilience, not off that many races this year. He executed it brilliantly’. — Photograph: Henry Nicholls/AFP/Getty Images

Source: The Guardian — Photos of the Day

item.description:
Cotignac, France — An aircraft flies past flames burning a forest surrounding Cotignac during a wildfire. The severity of fires in the EU has broken records for this time of year, data from the European Forest Fire Information System showed on Wednesday, and about twice as much land had burned by 22 July than the average for that date over the last two decades. France has broken records for the area burned; it and Spain have broken records for the number of fires. — Photograph: Thibaud Moritz/AFP/Getty Images

Source: The Guardian — Photos of the Day

Pontevès, France — Firefighters spray water as a wildfire flares up again in Pontevès. France has endured three almost back-to-back heatwaves since May as climate breakdown leads to more frequent and extreme weather events causing thousands of excess deaths, evaporating soils and waterways and fuelling wildfires. — Photograph: Thibaud Moritz/AFP/Getty Images

Ukrainian drones have hit at least nine Wildberries warehouses on four of the past seven days, striking logistics centres from southern Russia to the outskirts of St Petersburg, killing at least nine people and destroying inventory worth billions of dollars. — Photograph: AP

item.title: [The Atlantic — Photography] Photos: 50 Years Since Viking 1 Landed on Mars
item.description:
NASA — Viking 1 obtained this color picture of the Martian surface and sky on July 24, 1976. Camera No. 1, facing southeast, captured part of the gray structured spacecraft in the foreground. It was obtained by Viking 1 just minutes after the spacecraft landed successfully early today, July 20, 1976. The center of the image is about 1.4 meters (five feet) from Viking Lander camera #2. We see both rocks and finely granulated material—sand or dust. Many of the small foreground rocks are flat with angular facets. Several larger rocks exhibit irregular surfaces with pits and the large rock at top left shows intersecting linear cracks … At right is a portion of footpad #2. Small quantities of fine grained sand and dust are seen at the center of the footpad near the strut and were deposited at landing.”

Source: The Atlantic — Photography

item.title: [The Atlantic — Photography] Photos: 50 Years Since Viking 1 Landed on Mars
item.description:
NASA — The “face” on Mars. NASA’s Viking 1 Orbiter spacecraft photographed this region in the northern latitudes of Mars on July 25, 1976, while searching for a landing site for the Viking 2 Lander. The speckled appearance of the image is due to missing data, called bit errors, caused by problems in transmission of the photographic data from Mars to Earth. Bit errors comprise part of one of the “eyes” and “nostrils” on the eroded rock that resembles a human face near the center of the image. Shadows in the rock formation give the illusion of a nose and mouth. Planetary geologists attribute the origin of the formation to purely natural processes. More recent, higher-quality images of the same rock can be seen here.

Source: The Atlantic — Photography

item.description:
Buenos Aires, Argentina — Fans climb on a bus stop in Buenos Aires after Argentina’s victory over England in the World Cup semi-final. Argentina dug deep in the closing stages of the match to complete one of their greatest fightbacks. That it came against England, the old enemy, made it even sweeter. — Photograph: Rodrigo Abd/AP

Source: The Guardian — Photos of the Day

item.description:
Arlington, Texas, US — France’s Désiré Doué covers his face at full-time after his side’s defeat against Spain in the World Cup semi-final at Dallas Stadium. The Spanish team collectively swamped the individual flair of France, whose front four had run amok earlier in the tournament but were reduced to faulty, spluttering components by a superbly oiled machine. — Photograph: Julio Cortez/AP

Source: The Guardian — Photos of the Day

item.description:
London, England — People play football on pitches with dried grass after three heatwaves so far this summer, at Hackney Marshes in north-east London. The UK’s climatic extremes are becoming increasingly normal, a report has found, with last year the hottest on record and further ‘unprecedented changes’ likely to break the record again soon. — Photograph: Justin Tallis/AFP/Getty Images
